relation_to_existing_argument: Preserves marginal-identification-check.json. The earlier two-separate-marginals route required equal slopes and distinct difficulties. This different route uses one marginal plus a within-person two-item joint probability, allowing unequal known positive slopes and even identical item calibrations.

source_context.qualification: The source uses fixed calibration in the analysis. The actual calibration file and empirical responses are unavailable, so this argument does not verify that every required calibration/support/observation assumption holds for those data. Our separation of population identification from finite-sample likelihood uniqueness remains explicit.

conditional_statement.measurement: Y1,Y2 are two distinct conditionally independent binary observations given theta; P(Y1=1|theta)=f(theta)=L(a1*theta-d1), P(Y2=1|theta)=g(theta)=L(a2*theta-d2), with known finite d1,d2 and known finite positive slopes. Reorder the two items so0<a2<=a1. If the source writes L(a_j*(theta-b_j)), set d_j=a_j*b_j.
conditional_statement.latent: theta=mu+sZ with Z standard normal, finite mu and s>0.
conditional_statement.observed_target: Population p=E[Y1]=E[f(theta)] and q=E[Y1Y2]=E[f(theta)g(theta)]. The joint equality requires conditional independence; two repeated labels of the same binary draw do not suffice.
conditional_statement.claim: The mapping(mu,s) to(p,q) is globally injective onR times(0,infinity) under these conditions. No difference between d1 and d2 or between slopes is required.

derivation.name: Fixed marginal determines a mean curve
derivation.argument: For every finite s>0,p(mu,s)=E f(mu+sZ) is continuous and strictly increasing in mu because fprime>0. Its limits as mu tends to minus/plus infinity are0/1. Hence every p in(0,1) defines one mu_p(s). The implicit derivative is mu_pprime(s)=-E[Z fprime]/E[fprime]. Differentiation is justified by fprime<=a1/4 and finite E|Z|; positive denominator yields localC1 curves that agree globally by uniqueness.

derivation.name: Derivative of the within-person joint probability
derivation.argument: Let h=fg and w_s(z)=fprime(mu_p(s)+sz)phi(z)/E[fprime]. Differentiating q along the fixed-p curve gives E[Z hprime]-E[hprime]E[Z fprime]/E[fprime] = E[fprime]Cov_w(Z,r(mu_p(s)+sZ)), where r=hprime/fprime.

derivation.name: Positive-slope ordering makes the ratio strictly increasing
derivation.strict_sign: With c=a2/a1 in(0,1],the bracket=(1-c)+2c(1-g)>0 because0<g<1. Also a2>0,0<f<1. Thus rprime(theta)>0 for every finite theta, including equal slopes. Since s>0,r(mu_p(s)+sZ) is strictly increasing inZ.
derivation.symbolic_validation: Independent chain-rule differentiation using fprime=a1*f*(1-f),gprime=a2*g*(1-g) equals the displayed expression exactly. Identical-calibration limit g=f,a2=a1 gives rprime=2*a1*f*(1-f)>0.

derivation.name: Integrability and strict covariance
derivation.argument: For unequal slopes r may be unbounded, so bounded-r reasoning would be invalid. Instead fprime*r=hprime=fprime*g+f*gprime satisfies0<hprime<=(a1+a2)/4. Thus E_w[r]=E[hprime]/E[fprime] and E_w[|Z|r]=E[|Z|hprime]/E[fprime] are finite, as is E_w|Z|. The independent-copy identity Cov_w(Z,r(Z))=E[(Z-Zprime)(r(Z)-r(Zprime))]/2 is therefore valid. Weight w has positive density on allR and r is strictly increasing, making this covariance strictly positive.

derivation.name: Global identification of latent mean and variance
derivation.argument: Consequently q(mu_p(s),s) is strictly increasing over the connected domain s>0. Two parameter vectors with equalp andq must have equals and then equalmu. This is global injectivity, not just a nonsingular Jacobian at one point.

derivation.name: Cross-twin covariance and ACE bridge
derivation.argument: After mean and T=s^2 are identified at a fixed moderator level, a cross-twin item joint probability is strictly increasing in latent covarianceK for|K|<T: its derivative equals E[fjprime(theta1)*fkprime(theta2)]>0. The Gaussian identity partial_Kphi=partial_xpartial_yphi, followed by two justified integrations byparts, is unchanged by known positive unequal slopes since logistic factors and derivatives are bounded. MZ/DZ covariances then yield A=2(KMZ-KDZ),C=2KDZ-KMZ,E=T-KMZ. Two moderator levels recover all logvariance and mean coefficients.
derivation.required_joint_support: Both MZ andDZ groups must have positive observed support at EACH of the two distinct moderator levels. Within-person p/q and cross-twin item probabilities must be identifiable at those levels. Positive marginal support alone is insufficient.
derivation.other_bridge_assumptions: Same finite Gaussian mean/variance across zygosity at each shared moderator level; finite strictlypositive ACE; known genetic correlations1/.5; fixed invariant calibration and conditional measurement independence. The previously reviewed explicit inversion and support limits remain applicable.

boundary_and_scope_checks.finding: Allowed for two distinct conditionally independent item draws; q is the second conditional-probability moment, not a duplicate of p.

boundary_and_scope_checks.case: Only one observed item or joint item probability unavailable
boundary_and_scope_checks.finding: This argument cannot identify(mu,s) from p alone; it makes no automatic claim about other available response moments.
Then E[Y1Y2] need not equalE[fg]; proof fails unless a specified dependence model supplies an alternative identifiable relation.
Excluded from this positive-slope statement. Zero-slope item cannot supply the strict derivative; no blanket negative-slope extension asserted.
The displayed derivative need not remain positive if a2>a1. Relabeling is essential and always possible for two known positive slopes.

boundary_and_scope_checks.case: s=0,zero variancecomponents or singular twin covariance
boundary_and_scope_checks.finding: Outside the stated positive interior. No separate boundary theorem is asserted.
Excluded. Numerical saturation does not establish mathematical nonidentification.
Known finite calibration anchors trait scale/location. Unknown parameters can restore location/scale invariances and need explicit constraints and separate arguments.

Unequal known positive slopes alone are no longer an obstacle to this conditional argument. Actual positive calibration, jointly observed moments/support, latent Gaussian specification and missingness/ascertainment assumptions still require evidence; no empirical refit or model-validity claim.
Population injectivity neither gives finite-sample MLE existence/uniqueness nor posterior unimodality/convergence. The existing all-zero-response MLE counterexample remains compatible.
